SUNDAY RUN, AND A BOOK-HYGIENE REPORT RATHER THAN AN IDEA REPORT. Six of the eight lines below are position management on the existing book — two full closes (LULU, NKE), one netting fix (TLT), two amendments (GLD target cut, SPY stop widened) and one bear case added (CCJ). Only BTC is a new idea, and XLE is a fix to a pending line that is now 0.25% from its entry. That is what the research found, not a shortfall against a quota.

PRICES. Every equity figure is the Friday 2026-09-04 close (finnhub, session=closed, ~38h old). At 6am ET on a Sunday that is the freshest honest price, not stale data. Monday 2026-09-07 is Labor Day, so the next equity session is Tuesday 2026-09-08 and every equity instruction below is written for that open. BTC is a live 24/7 quote (79,962 at 06:45 ET).

RESEARCH WAS NOT TRUNCATED — a RESEARCH COMPLETE block was logged at 06:27 ET after ~27 minutes.

SOURCE FAILURES. (1) Yahoo chart API returned HTTP 429 on every index symbol, so there is NO VIX, no index quote, no futures quote and no DXY in this report; ETF proxies were used instead. (2) Yahoo options returned 401 on every name, so no idea carries the 'is my target inside the market-implied move' check — ORCL and ADBE were rejected partly for that reason. (3) api.nasdaq.com timed out on short interest for NKE, LULU and CCJ, so one positioning input is missing from every equity idea and conviction scores are lower than they would otherwise be. (4) REPO BUG: scripts/market_data.py events() reads Kalshi's old field names (yes_bid, last_price, volume, open_interest); Kalshi now returns yes_bid_dollars / last_price_dollars / volume_fp / open_interest_fp, so every event contract reads null through the CLI. Research worked around it by calling the markets endpoint directly. This needs fixing in the repo.

ZERO EVENT CONTRACTS, deliberately. The Fed strip was checked for arbitrage against the cumulative funds-ceiling ladder and agrees to within 0.01 expected hikes by December — an arbitraged complex, not a mispricing. September is a 49.5/48.5 coin flip and there is no stated probability disagreement to trade. The CPI ladders' only two monotonicity violations die on the spread, and the tradeable CPI strikes are quoted 5-8c wide on a Sunday (~15% of position value to cross). KXBTC/KXETH/KXINX ladders have effectively zero open interest. No idea beats manufacturing one.

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, which matters more than any single idea: all 8 pending LONGS in the book are unfilled and the market is ABOVE every one of them — VST +16.6%, PFE +10.3%, DG +10.1%, CEG +9.9%, LCII +9.2%, DINO +5.9%, EEM +4.7%, XLE +0.3%, mean +8.4%. The theses were right and the entries were wrong: each was a reflex limit below the last print, and the market never came back. For the five names now 9-17% through their entries the honest choice is enter at market on a re-underwritten thesis or cancel the line; there was no budget to re-underwrite five theses today, so they are on the watchlist as a structural flag rather than re-pitched. The BTC idea below is a stop-limit BREAKOUT entry and the two exits use limits BELOW market precisely because of this table.

THREE NETTING ERRORS IN ONE BOOK, all the same failure: TLT held long and short simultaneously with the two stops bracketing spot; YES on both 'Fed hikes in September' and 'Fed holds in September'; and a stale bearish BTC pair still pending against the BTC long pitched today. merge_report dedupes on (symbol, direction) and so cannot see an opposing pair — that is a process gap worth a test in tests/.

RATIOS. Four of the six priced ideas land at 2.02-2.19 against a 2.0 swing floor, which is the clustering signature of targets fitted to clear a bar, so it is flagged here on principle. What the research log actually shows is the opposite direction of travel: SPY's stop was WIDENED from 782.00 to 783.50 because 1.64 ATR sat under the 1.8 ETF floor, cutting its ratio from 2.56 to 2.19, and TLT's 83.60 stop was explicitly left alone. Nothing was tightened to clear a ratio anywhere in this run, and every stop was checked in ATRs: TLT 2.61, SPY 1.91, BTC 2.58, XLE 2.00, against floors of 1.8/1.8/2.5/1.8.

GLD FAILS ITS FLOOR ON PURPOSE. At a 448 target against a 368 bear case it returns 1.67:1, under the 2.5 long-term floor. It is published anyway because it is an amendment to a filled position, not new risk: the prior 520 target rested on a factual error (gold was described as record-area when GLD is 20.2% below its January high), and the correct action is hold-and-trim with no adds at any price. It would not publish if proposed fresh today, and the thesis says so.

NOT DONE. The uranium (CCJ) and energy (DINO) theses were not re-underwritten this run — CCJ's update is position management only. BCC shows +3.5% against its entry here but prior_context reports -2.2%; that discrepancy is unreconciled and flagged rather than guessed at. BCC and SVRA are both holds with no new information, so no recommendation is emitted for either.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Eight ideas in, five out. Cut LULU and NKE from the recommendation list and TLT's long leg with them — not because the cases are weak (LULU's is the best-evidenced item in the report) but because THE PIPELINE HAS NO CLOSE VERB. positions_from_report() keys on (symbol, direction), so a `sell` row against a live `buy` does not close it: it would have opened phantom LULU and NKE SHORTS at 98.00 and 37.90 with null targets and null stops, while leaving both longs standing with their 180.00 and 62.00 targets and no stop. Verified by running the merge against state/open_positions.json. All three closes now sit on the watchlist in full and must be executed by hand. Cut GLD, taking it at its own word — it states it 'would not publish if proposed fresh today' and returns 1.67:1 against the 2.5 long-term floor. Its 520 -> 448 target cut is preserved in the watchlist note; because merge_report() reads only `recommendations`, the open GLD long keeps the fantasy 520.00 target until someone edits state by hand. Downgraded four of the five survivors: TLT 4 -> 3 (its own counter_argument documents a FAILED catalyst — the maximally bond-bearish print available and TLT closed UP — on the thinnest claimed edge in the book, 5.3 points), XLE 4 -> 3 (the OPEC+ pause was reported before the meeting, so it is public, and the name has already run +10.14% in a month to 2.23% off a 250-day high), SPY 4 -> 3 (one of its three evidence kinds justifies where the stop goes rather than confirming the index falls, and a second is verbatim the TLT short's), BTC 3 -> 2 with size cut 2% -> 1% (its second evidence kind is the FOMC, which its own key_risk names as a HEADWIND — a catalyst that works against the trade is not a confirmation of it). CCJ left at 3 unchanged. NOTHING had its target moved out to rescue a ratio, and no stop was walked in. CORRELATION: TLT short and SPY short are one hawkish-FOMC bet wearing two tickers — same catalyst, same evidence sentence — and should be sized as one 4% macro position. BTC long and SPY short are opposite risk-appetite bets keyed to that same 2026-09-16 event. WHAT SURVIVED VERIFICATION. LULU's evidence was re-read against the 8-K Ex-99.1 itself and every figure matches; two of the report's own statements understated its case and are corrected in the watchlist note (the $9.48-9.73 FY guide INCLUDES $0.86/share of non-recurring tariff refunds, so the multiple is 11.3-11.7x rather than 10.3-10.6x; and the issuer states the refund raised gross margin by 560bp, so ex-refund gross margin FELL ~360bp). BTC's arithmetic was re-derived from the CoinGecko series and is exactly right (ATR14 2,327, 30-day high 82,108, all eight coiling closes reproduce). NKE's order logic was inverted and is fixed: a sell limit at 37.90 against a 38.40 close is marketable and fails to fill ONLY if the stock breaks the 37.95 250-day low — the opposite of what the report said a non-fill would mean. REPO BUG FOUND AND FIXED. validate_report.check_sources probed sources with HEAD only, and api.nasdaq.com and the Kalshi markets endpoint both answer HEAD with 404 while serving 200 on GET. That is why all 8 ideas read `fail`: six failed on `sources` and nothing else. Unfixed, phase 2d --enforce would have demoted every surviving recommendation and published an empty report on a false signal. A HEAD 404 is now confirmed with a GET before a source is called dead; five tests added in tests/test_validate_report.py, full suite green (601). One genuinely dead URL was found and replaced — the Robinhood crypto support article cited by the BTC idea 404s on GET too. REPO ISSUES LEFT OPEN, both real and neither worked around here. (1) No close verb, as above — three closes today could not be expressed as recommendations. (2) An amendment that honestly CUTS a target on a losing position is blocked by the reward-to-risk floor, which exists to gate new ideas; GLD's correction of a factual error is the casualty, and the alternative is that a position must keep an unreachable target forever. (3) XLE and BTC carry catalyst.wait = true, so positions_from_report() skips them and their amended levels never reach state — which means the stale pending XLE long at 63.90/70.50/60.80, the resting limit the XLE idea exists to cancel, survives this run untouched. Cancel it by hand before Tuesday's open; a buy limit below the market fills exactly when the OPEC+ news is bad.

RED TEAM: conviction cut 4 -> 3 on the priced-in test. The stop is a second mark against the score: 2.00 ATR clears the 1.8 floor but sits under the 2.25 level where this report's stop-outs have clustered, so the 2.19:1 is flattered by a stop that may not survive normal noise.

recommendations.thesis: Bitcoin has spent eight sessions coiling in a 77,270-81,752 band directly beneath the 82,108 thirty-day high, after rising 31% from 62,525 over the prior month. The trade is the resolution of that coil, not the coil itself: a stop-limit above the high, so the position only exists if the range breaks upward, with the stop below the consolidation floor rather than inside it. This is deliberately a breakout entry — the first month of this report ran 31 pullback entries against 1 breakout, filled 42% of them, and the ones that filled were the ones already falling.
recommendations.key_risk: A breakout above a month-long high that immediately reverses is the most common failure of this structure, and crypto gaps through stops over weekends with no halts — the 2.5 ATR crypto floor exists because of that and the stop still may not hold. The FOMC is a genuine two-sided risk: a hike on 2026-09-16 lifts real rates, which is a headwind for a non-yielding asset, and this idea requires the breakout to happen anyway. PIPELINE WARNING: catalyst.wait = true, so this idea is skipped by positions_from_report() and nothing is recorded in state/open_positions.json this run. Correct — nothing was entered — but if the 82,108 breakout triggers before the next run, the fill will not be tracked.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that buying a 30-day high after a 31% month is buying the top of the move rather than the start of one, and 82,108 is also close to the 82,751 six-month high, so the breakout has a second ceiling immediately above it. The answer is structural rather than predictive: the entry is conditional, so if the range holds nothing is bought; and the 94,500 target sits in open space above the entire six-month range, which is why a measured move from the 19,583-point base projects to 101,691 rather than into overhead supply. RED TEAM: conviction cut 3 -> 2 and size cut 2% -> 1% (the conviction-2 cap). The arithmetic was re-derived independently from the CoinGecko series and is exactly right — ATR14 2,327, 30-day high 82,108, 30-day low 62,525, all eight coiling closes reproduce, stop 2.58 ATR, 2.02:1 — so this is not a numbers objection. It is an evidence objection: conviction 3 needs two independent confirmations, and the second one listed is the FOMC, which this idea's own key_risk names as a HEADWIND ('a hike lifts real rates, which is a headwind for a non-yielding asset'). A catalyst the thesis says works against the trade is not a confirmation of it. Strip it and one kind remains — technical_level — which supports 2. Note also that this long and the SPY short are opposite risk-appetite bets keyed to the same 2026-09-16 event.

Same container problem as LULU: a `sell` row does not close the (NKE, buy) long, it opens a phantom NKE short at 37.90 with null target and null stop and leaves the 62.00-target long standing. Close by hand. ORDER LOGIC CORRECTED — the report's stated rationale was backwards. A sell limit at 37.90 against a 38.40 close is marketable: it fills at the open at 38.40-ish for any price at or above 37.90. It fails to fill ONLY if the stock trades BELOW 37.90, i.e. only if NKE has BROKEN the 37.95 250-day low — the opposite of the report's 'if the exit does not fill the stock has held its low'. A non-fill is therefore a bearish signal, not a reason to reconsider the close. Use a plain market order on the Tue 2026-09-08 open, or keep the 37.90 limit understanding that a non-fill means the low broke. The substance stands and is not in dispute: all five open-market insider buys are 2026-04-07 to 04-13 at 42.27-43.34, five months stale and every one underwater; NKE lags SPY by 47.19% and XLY by 33.05% over six months; and at an honest 48 target against a 33 bear case the position returns 0.63:1, far under the 2.5 long-term floor.
